input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts from the preferred position (Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio, with Commerce One assigning any claim it may have, and Commerce One retaining its pre-existing technology under 2.8 — vendor platform ownership is acceptable). However, the "unless" carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to Corio. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and fails even the fallback (which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use the deliverables), so it is walk-away territory on a critical term. The smallest edit to reach the preferred position is deletion of the carve-out; if Commerce One needs rights in Developments it maintains, a licence from Corio rather than ownership is the sensible fallback. Noted but not separately flagged: the final sentence of 13.5 leaves ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation (no joint ownership is created), and the agreement has no Customer Data ownership sentence, a minor sub-element in this hosting/reseller structure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that transfers ownership of Developments created solely by Corio to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, since our playbook does not permit any assignment of our IP or work product to a vendor, and the carve-out gave us no licence back. If Commerce One needs rights in Developments it maintains, we can instead grant it a licence to those Developments while ownership stays with Corio.
proposal.summary: Remove vendor ownership carve-out so Corio owns all Developments it creates.
